title: SkillFormer: Unified Multi-View Video Understanding for Proficiency Estimation
tldr: Fuse the performer's own view with the outside views through cross-attention and LoRA, and proficiency estimation gets better while using 4.5× fewer parameters.

problem.task: Estimate how skilled the performer is, from synchronized egocentric and exocentric video.

inputs.name: multi-view video
inputs.chars: Ego-Exo4D structured activities — bouldering, cooking, music, basketball.

training.supervision: Proficiency labels from Ego-Exo4D; only a LoRA subset of parameters is updated.
training.note: 3.75× fewer training epochs than prior baselines, which matters because multi-view models are usually the expensive option.

method.intuition: Each viewpoint sees a different part of the skill, so fuse them adaptively rather than picking one or averaging.

experiments.headline: State-of-the-art multi-view accuracy on Ego-Exo4D with 4.5× fewer parameters and 3.75× fewer training epochs.

why: Judging skill is the prerequisite for coaching it, and this is the cheapest current way to do it across views.

title: Generating Physically Stable and Buildable Brick Structures from Text
tldr: Generate a brick model one brick at a time, and prune each candidate token against gravity and assembly constraints, so the output is something a hand or an arm can actually build.

problem.task: Text to a physically stable, buildable interconnecting brick assembly.

outputs.name: brick sequence
outputs.chars: Next-brick prediction; each brick is a placement token.

outputs.name: assembly
outputs.chars: Verified stable, and assembled in practice by hand and by a robot arm.

training.supervision: StableText2Brick: 47,000+ physically stable structures over 28,000+ unique 3D objects with captions.
training.note: Physics enters at inference as a rollback that prunes infeasible tokens, so stability is enforced rather than hoped for.

method.intuition: A generative model will happily emit a structure that falls over, so put the physics check inside the decoding loop rather than after it.

experiments.headline: Stable, diverse structures that match the prompt, assembled both by hand and automatically by robotic arms.

why: The one paper here whose output is matter. Generation with a buildability constraint is what separates design from physical AI.

title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
tldr: Training environments are hand-built, blind to where the agent is weak, and obsolete once it improves. Wrap them in a layer that reads the agent's failures and reshapes the world around them.

problem.task: Reshape an existing environment, through its own interface, to target the failures of the policy training in it.

inputs.name: static environment
inputs.chars: Any existing environment, reached through its standard interface, so its verifier survives.

inputs.name: policy trajectories
inputs.chars: The target policy is a black box; only its behaviour is read.

outputs.name: harness components
outputs.chars: Plug-in modifications aimed at diagnosed weaknesses, validated by fresh rollouts.

training.supervision: EnvRigger synthesizes and validates components; the harness also serves as an RL reward signal.
training.note: Policy and environment co-evolve, which is the adapt stage of the loop applied to the world rather than the model.

method.intuition: Rebuilding an environment per domain is the engineering cost that kills environment generation, so wrap instead of rebuild and keep the original verifier.
method.backbone: LLM component synthesizer over environment interfaces

experiments.headline: Up to +9.0 points on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps, beating both the original environments and domain-specific generation pipelines.

why: The rare paper where the thing being adapted is the environment, which is what a physical curriculum would have to look like.

title: EgoDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Large-Scale Egocentric Video
tldr: 829 hours of egocentric video with every finger joint tracked at recording time, because Apple Vision Pro can do the tracking that Ego4D never had.

problem.task: Hand trajectory prediction from egocentric video, as a stand-in for dexterous imitation at internet scale.

inputs.name: egocentric video
inputs.chars: 194 tabletop tasks, from tying shoelaces to folding laundry.

outputs.name: 3D hand and finger trajectory
outputs.chars: Every joint of each hand, tracked by on-device SLAM plus calibrated cameras rather than estimated post hoc.

training.supervision: Paired video and hand pose, captured simultaneously.
training.note: Native pose annotation is the difference from Ego4D — no downstream hand estimator in the loop, so the labels do not inherit its errors.

method.intuition: Dexterous manipulation has no internet-scale corpus, and the cheapest way to make one is to record the hands with hardware that already tracks them.
components: 829 h of paired video and 3D hand tracking
hand trajectory prediction benchmark and metrics

baselines: imitation learning policies trained on the dataset
experiments.headline: The largest and most diverse dexterous human manipulation dataset to date, with a systematic evaluation of trajectory-prediction policies on it.

why: The clearest example of the human-video-as-robot-data bet, and the one with the fewest annotation caveats.

title: Web2Grasp: Learning Functional Grasps from Web Images of Hand-Object Interactions
tldr: Photographs of people holding things already encode how to hold them for use, which is the half a power grasp misses. Reconstruct those grasps in 3D, filter by physics, and train a hand on the survivors.

problem.task: Functional multi-finger grasping of everyday objects, learned without in-domain demonstrations.

inputs.name: object
inputs.chars: Including unseen and awkward ones — syringe, spray bottle, knife, tongs.

outputs.name: hand configuration
outputs.chars: A grasp that supports use, not only holding.

training.supervision: 3D hand-object meshes reconstructed from web RGB images by a pretrained model, then filtered.
training.note: Two filters make the noisy data usable: geometric feasibility, then physical simulation under disturbance.

method.intuition: Power grasps are easy and useless. Functional grasps are what people photograph themselves doing, so mine those.

experiments.headline: 75.8% success in simulation on web-dataset objects with generalization to unseen ones, and 77.5% across 12 real objects on two hands.

why: Web images as a source of physical priors, which is the cheapest end of the human-data-to-robot spectrum.

title: TI-PREGO: Chain of Thought and In-Context Learning for Online Mistake Detection in Procedural Egocentric Videos
tldr: Same recognize-and-anticipate mismatch as PREGO, but the anticipation branch is an LLM doing in-context pattern matching over action tokens.

problem.task: Open-set online mistake detection with no examples of failure.

inputs.name: egocentric frames
inputs.chars: Streaming; per-frame evaluation is benchmarked explicitly, which earlier work skipped.

outputs.name: mistake flag
outputs.chars: Mismatch between the recognized action token and the anticipated one.

training.supervision: Recognition is trained; anticipation is in-context, so no failure examples are needed anywhere.
training.note: Aggregating frame-level predictions into action tokens is what makes the LLM branch usable online.

method.intuition: Next-step anticipation over a procedure is sequence pattern matching, and an LLM does that in context without being trained on the task.
method.backbone: step recognition branch + LLM anticipation branch

experiments.headline: Improves online open-set mistake detection over PREGO and documents how hard per-frame evaluation actually is.

why: The follow-up that shows how much of the mistake-detection loop can be moved into a frozen language model.

title: Modeling Multiple Normal Action Representations for Error Detection in Procedural Tasks
tldr: After any given prefix there are usually several correct next actions. Detectors that hold one static prototype per step call the other correct ones errors.

problem.task: Detect execution errors by comparing the ongoing action against every action that would have been valid here.

outputs.name: valid next actions
outputs.chars: All of them, not the single most likely one.

outputs.name: error score
outputs.chars: Distance from the ongoing action to the nearest reconstructed normal representation.

training.supervision: Correct executions; representations are reconstructed per predicted valid action rather than stored as fixed prototypes.
training.note: Adaptivity is what survives a shift between the training and deployment distribution.

method.intuition: A static prototype assumes one right answer per step, and procedures rarely have one, so the comparison target has to be predicted afresh each time.

experiments.headline: State-of-the-art error detection, with ablations isolating the gain from modeling multiple valid next actions.

why: Names the failure mode a deployed task assistant would hit first: punishing a user for doing it a different correct way.

title: I²G: Generating Instructional Illustrations via Text-Conditioned Diffusion
tldr: Text cannot carry a spatial relationship. Parse the instruction into goal and steps, condition generation on that structure, and the illustrations stay coherent across the sequence.

problem.task: Turn procedural text into a coherent sequence of instructional illustrations.

inputs.name: procedural text
inputs.chars: Decomposed by a constituency parser, so long instructions keep their semantics.

outputs.name: illustration sequence
outputs.chars: Consistent across steps, matched against a purpose-built alignment protocol.

training.note: A pairwise discourse-coherence model enforces consistency between consecutive steps rather than per-image quality.

method.intuition: The failure in text-to-image for instructions is discourse, not rendering, so model the linguistic structure of the procedure explicitly.

experiments.headline: Outperforms existing baselines on all three instructional datasets for content accuracy and sequential consistency.

why: The generation side of visual guidance, with the evaluation problem taken seriously rather than eyeballed.

title: Enhancing User Performance and Human Factors through Visual Guidance in AR Assembly Tasks
tldr: AR guidance cut assembly time 31% and raised the error rate at the same time. Speed and accuracy trade against each other, and most guidance papers only report one.

problem.task: Measure how different supportive visualizations change assembly performance and human factors.

inputs.name: visualization condition
inputs.chars: Types of supportive visualization, varied between subjects; occlusion is manipulated by design.

training.note: Prior AR guidance studies varied interaction method; this varies the visualization itself, which is why the results are less muddled.

method.intuition: The literature disagrees about whether AR guidance helps because it keeps changing the wrong variable.
components: cognitive load, motivation and usability measures

experiments.headline: 31% faster completion, offset by a significant rise in errors — a speed-accuracy trade-off that single-metric evaluations hide.

why: The empirical check on every AR guidance system on this list: faster is not automatically better.

title: avaTTAR: Table Tennis Stroke Training with On-body and Detached Visualization in Augmented Reality
tldr: Show the target stroke on the learner's own body and beside it at the same time, so they can both feel the correction and see it from outside.

problem.task: Real-time stroke correction in AR against an expert reference.

inputs.name: learner motion
inputs.chars: Pose estimation plus IMU on the paddle.

outputs.name: dual-view overlay
outputs.chars: First-person overlay on the learner's own limbs, plus a third-person avatar beside them.

training.supervision: None — comparison against recorded expert strokes.
training.note: The two viewpoints answer different questions, which is why offering both beats choosing one.

method.intuition: A correction shown only in first person is hard to see and one shown only in third person is hard to map onto your own body.

datasets.name: user study with table tennis players

experiments.headline: Improved player experience and training results in a user study.

why: Shows the change channel of visual guidance being designed around the human's viewpoint, which the model-side papers rarely consider.

title: SneakPeek: Future-Guided Instructional Streaming Video Generation
tldr: Streaming a multi-step demonstration drifts because each frame is generated blind to the step after next. Anticipate future keyframes and generate toward them.

problem.task: Generate a stepwise instructional video, streaming, from an initial image and structured step prompts.

inputs.name: multi-step prompts
inputs.chars: One per procedural step, giving fine-grained control over the sequence.

outputs.name: streaming video
outputs.chars: Interactive — future steps can be changed while generation runs.

training.supervision: Causal adaptation of a diffusion model to next-frame prediction plus future keyframe anticipation.
training.note: Dual-region KV caching addresses exposure bias, which is the specific reason long autoregressive rollouts drift.

method.intuition: An instructional demonstration has a known destination, so let the generator see the destination instead of only the last frame.
components: future-guided self-forcing with dual-region KV cache

experiments.headline: Mitigates temporal drift and preserves motion consistency across long multi-step sequences, with interactive control over what comes next.

why: The streaming regime applied to the visual-guidance channel, which is what an on-glasses demonstration would need.

title: Ego-EXTRA: video-language Egocentric Dataset for EXpert-TRAinee assistance
tldr: A real expert plays the wearable assistant, seeing only the trainee's first-person view. 50 hours of that gives you what expert-level guidance sounds like.

problem.task: Visual question answering that stands in for expert-level task assistance.

inputs.name: trainee question
inputs.chars: Asked mid-task, as it actually comes out.

outputs.name: expert answer
outputs.chars: 15k+ high-quality VQA sets drawn from the recorded two-way dialogue.

training.supervision: Wizard-of-Oz collection: a human expert enacts the assistant, restricted to the trainee's egocentric view.
training.note: The restriction is what makes the transcript a valid target — the expert had exactly the information a wearable would have.

method.intuition: You cannot train an expert assistant without a record of expert assistance, and the only honest way to record it is to give a real expert the assistant's sensory limits.

experiments.headline: Challenging for current MLLMs, exposing their limits when asked to provide expert-level assistance.

why: The successor to HoloAssist's premise, with the expert's information restricted to what a wearable would actually see.

title: Generating Dialogues from Egocentric Instructional Videos for Task Assistance: Dataset, Method and Benchmark
tldr: Human-collected guidance dialogue is expensive, so synthesize it: turn single-person how-to videos into two-person teaching conversations aligned to the steps.

problem.task: Multi-turn task-guidance dialogue grounded in a wearable's video and audio.

outputs.name: expert turn
outputs.chars: Step-aligned teaching, one turn at a time.

training.supervision: HowToDIV: 507 conversations, 6,636 QA pairs, 24 hours of clips across cooking, mechanics and planting, generated automatically by LLMs from single-person video.
training.note: Synthetic dialogue trades fidelity for scale, which is the trade Ego-EXTRA makes in the other direction.

method.intuition: The scarce resource is dialogue, not video, and an LLM can manufacture the missing half of the conversation from an existing demonstration.
components: automatic single-video to two-person dialogue conversion

experiments.headline: 507 conversations and 24 hours of clips built with no human-assisted collection, plus a baseline for the new task.

why: Read next to Ego-EXTRA: the same task, one dataset synthesized and one recorded, which is the cleanest available comparison of that choice.

title: Emergent Active Perception and Dexterity of Simulated Humanoids from Visual Reinforcement Learning
tldr: Take away privileged object positions and give a humanoid only its own eyes, and searching for things emerges by itself.

problem.task: Whole-body dexterous control of a simulated humanoid from egocentric vision only.

inputs.name: egocentric render
inputs.chars: The only task specification. No 3D object positions, no geometry.

outputs.name: whole-body action
outputs.chars: One policy covering reaching, grasping, placing and articulated manipulation.

training.supervision: Reinforcement learning from scratch on visual observation.
training.note: Removing privileged state is the experimental manipulation; active search is what appears when you do.

method.intuition: Human movement is shaped by having to look for what it needs, so a policy that must gather its own information should develop the same behaviours.

metrics: task success across reaching, grasping, placing, articulated manipulation
experiments.headline: One policy performs multiple household tasks from vision alone, with active search emerging from training rather than being engineered.

why: The perception-action loop closed inside a single policy, and the strongest argument here that perception is an action.

title: LATMOS: Latent Automaton Task Model from Observation Sequences
tldr: Learn an automaton whose symbols live in a latent feature space, and one model factorizes the task, verifies an execution and plans the next step.

problem.task: Learn a task model from correct executions that supports factorization, planning and verification at once.

inputs.name: observation sequence
inputs.chars: Logical formulas, human task video with prompts, or robot images and states — three setups, one model.

outputs.name: latent automaton state
outputs.chars: Symbols live in the encoder's feature space rather than a hand-written vocabulary.

training.note: Automata give verification for free, which most learned task models cannot do.

method.intuition: Task planning needs factorization, state estimation and verification together, and an automaton with learned symbols gives all three in one object.

datasets.name: real human task videos with prompts

baselines: learned task models without automaton structure
experiments.headline: Improved plan generation and verification across all three setups, from abstract formulas to a real robot task.

why: The neuro-symbolic middle of the procedure axis: learned features, but a structure you can check a plan against.

title: Evaluating the Effects of Situated and Embedded Visualisation in Augmented Reality Guidance for Isolated Medical Assistance
tldr: When the nearest expert is a continent away, the question is where to put the instruction: on the patient, or projected beside them. 23 novices, two conditions.

problem.task: Compare embedded visualization against situated projected visualization for AR-guided medical procedures.

inputs.name: visualization condition
inputs.chars: Embedded sits on the object; situated is projected nearby.

outputs.name: performance and preference
outputs.chars: 23 participants with latent or novice medical knowledge.

training.note: The population is chosen to match the real case — trained but out of practice, and out of reach of help.

method.intuition: Guidance for an isolated operator has to promote autonomy, and where the information sits in the physical world decides whether it does.

datasets.name: controlled AR medical guidance study, N=23

experiments.headline: A direct comparison of embedded against situated projected AR guidance for medical procedures performed without expert help.

why: The clinical end of visual guidance, where the operator is alone and the cost of a wrong instruction is highest.
